metrics.result:
I added a 9:16 version to `film.reel`, and the headline now fits. I checked a frame of each format, and the lint shows no errors. The three warnings that remain are text-density, static-end and, for 16:9 only, a safe-area warning on the headline.

**What changed:** the headline was set to stay on one line, which at 110 px is far wider than a 1080 px-wide story frame. The header now lists `formats=[16:9, 9:16]`, and the headline is allowed to wrap. Landscape still shows it on one line, as before. In portrait it breaks into three centered lines at a larger size (130 px). I also nudged the headline and subline positions in portrait.

**Renders**, both 6 seconds:
- `out/film-16x9.mp4` is 1920×1080.
- `out/film-9x16.mp4` is 1080×1920.

The 16:9 headline now has a 92% text box instead of staying on one line regardless of width. It still renders on one line, but its edges sit about 85 px from the frame. That's what triggers the safe-area warning, and I left it as is.

I didn't check the 9:16 frame against the platform UI band at the bottom 20%. The text sits well above it.

checklist.item: vertical version: the headline fits inside the frame (wraps or scales)
checklist.evidence: Headline wraps to 3 lines in 9:16 with clear margins on both sides, nothing clipped.

checklist.item: landscape version still looks as before
checklist.evidence: 16:9 headline on one line, subline below, same layout, colours and positions as the original.
Both formats show 'OPEN DAY AT THE MAKERSPACE' and 'Saturday 10:00 to 16:00, free entry' unchanged.

problems: Vertical layout leaves the bottom ~50% of the frame empty; the content sits in the upper-middle, so the frame is poorly used.
Subline is small in vertical (about 44px on 1080 width), so it is hard to read on a phone.
Vertical text sits at roughly 30-55% height, and the Stories UI may crowd the top and bottom; the placement is acceptable but not tuned.
Design is plain: text on a gradient with no accent or graphic, and there is little motion after the intro.
judge.verdict: The edit does what was asked. The vertical headline now wraps to three lines and fits with margins, the landscape version looks the same as before, and the copy is unchanged. The vertical frame has a lot of empty space below the text, and the subline is small. Both are minor, and the layout is plain but clean.
